rounds.text: Vijay Solvex Ltd carries fundamental and valuation risks that are not fully erased by its headline discount to book value [E2]. The business suffers from severe cash burn, reporting an operating cash flow of Rs -61 Cr and a free cash flow of Rs -67 Cr in March 2026, leading to a dismal cash conversion of -3.21x against reported profits [E34, E35, E36]. This cash drain has forced borrowings upward from Rs 33 Cr to Rs 65 Cr within a single year [E39]. Furthermore, long-term growth has been anaemic, demonstrated by a 5-year compounded sales growth of just 3% and a 3-year contraction of -1%, alongside a 5-year compounded profit decline of -22% [E15, E16, E19]. Return metrics remain thoroughly depressed, with a 3-year median return on equity of just 4% and a current ROE of 6% [E28, E29], lagging far behind sector benchmarks [E9]. Valuation-wise, a discounted cash flow model places intrinsic value at Rs 656 per share, leaving a negative margin of safety of -5.2% against the current market price of Rs 690 [E43, E44]. Conceded: the company trades at a low price-to-book ratio of 0.69x and features a trailing twelve-month sales growth spurt of 29% [E2, E17].

The bear fixates on cash burn and rising borrowings without acknowledging that capital expenditure has essentially finished, evidenced by CWIP plunging -90.9% to just Rs 1 Cr as new capacity comes online [E40]. Conceded: operating cash flow hit Rs -61 Cr and borrowings rose to Rs 65 Cr [E35, E39]. However, dismissing the top-line performance overlooks a powerful recent acceleration, including a 29% trailing twelve-month sales growth spurt alongside a 44% year-over-year sales surge and a 68% jump in net profit [E17, E63, E65]. The bear leans on depressed historical return metrics, but a turnaround is actively underway with results scoring 100/100 and a bias check warning against dismissing accelerating momentum based on stale sentiment [E68]. Furthermore, the valuation discount is substantial: the stock trades at an ultra-low price-to-book of 0.69x against a sector benchmark of 3.17x, and an EV/EBITDA of 6.34x compared to the sector's 10.94x [E2, E7, E11]. Finally, management skin in the game is increasing rather than retreating, with promoter holdings rising by 1.94 percentage points to 69.59% [E41].
